rv.q: The cast digs deep into Arbery’s words and makes this an evening well worth your time.

Figueroa's staging makes the most of the small runway playing area (designed by Spencer Donovan) in the Den's Bookspan space, with Peter and Basil's office at one end and Jane's home on the other—and a cold, dark stretch of road and piles of dirty snow between work and homelife.
Blending absurdism with hyper-realism and humor, Arbery’s script is often confusing. But it also has enough humanity to keep everyone, characters and audience alike, from total despair.
There’s a lot to like about First Floor Theater’s production of Evanston Salt Costs Climbing.
What begins as a slightly quirky, workspace comedy quickly begins to reveal a darker core.
It’s an entertaining show and impossible to predict. It’s a fine day at the theater, though its artistic borrowing may ruffle feathers.
